answer: The cordwainer pegs the heel seat of every shoe he makes and enters the pair in his tally against the customer. A summit pair bought from another town fails the tally: at the mirror of the heel the pegging must match the cordwainer's own awl, and bought shoes pinch within a week. Forging a pair means hiring a cordwainer, buying false leather and paying 8,800, and the ocean entry in the heel-seat tally is read at every market, so shoes whose heel was never pegged are thrown out.
